A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WebCoderBench and contain 34 pages, including appendices A–F. Text extraction and rendered-page inspection support a complete comparison; pages 4–34 are visually identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 12 LLMs and two agents in Section 5, with results in Table 4 and Figure 5, plus a preference survey with 141 valid responses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original model evaluations, preference-survey results, and supplementary results and analyses in appendices B and C.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, 24 evaluation metrics, rule-based and LLM judging procedures, and preference-weighted aggregation remain unchanged, including their appendix specifications.

E1.justification: Both versions report the same 1,572 user requirements across 20 application categories, covering text-only, image-containing, and URL-containing inputs for native web front-end generation.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison set remains the same 12 LLMs and two agents, Manus and MiniMax Agent. Comparator membership is unchanged in Table 4 and appendix Tables 10–11.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 retains one artifact per requirement, the full dataset for LLMs, and 165 requirements for agents. Prompts, modality conversion, scoring procedures, and exclusion of unscorable cases are unchanged.

E4.justification: The question-type and user-persona analyses in Sections 5.3–5.4, metric-validation checks, and Appendix C's analysis of four categories of unscorable cases are identical.

E5.justification: Both Limitations sections report three runs of LLM-as-a-judge metrics on 50 requirements and Mann–Whitney U testing. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: All reported results are unchanged, including Tables 4–6, Figure 5, and appendix Tables 10–11. For example, Table 4 retains overall scores of 13.81% for GPT-5-High and 11.76% for GLM-4.5.

T1.justification: The z-score definition and weighting calculations in Section 4.3 and the metric formulas in Appendix A are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same benchmark novelty, interpretability, and human-preference alignment claims, including the finding that no model dominates all metrics.

C2.justification: Interpretations of model differences, requirement characteristics, and user preferences remain identical. Limitations concerning front-end scope, unavailable data and implementation, annotation reliability, and metric validity are also retained.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, questionnaire, annotation guidelines, and prompts in appendices A and D–F are unchanged. The results-access link and stated restrictions on releasing the dataset and evaluation implementation remain the same.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and comparison with existing benchmarks in Table 1 are unchanged. The corrected internal table reference does not alter research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds an equal-contribution note for Chenxu Liu and Yingjie Fu and adjusts author footnote markers. Section 3.2 corrects its dataset-statistics reference from Figure 2 to Table 2; the remaining narrative and organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added author footnote produces small text-flow shifts on pages 1–2, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Figures, tables, captions, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies equal-contribution attribution and corrects Section 3.2 to point to the statistics in Table 2 rather than the example in Figure 2. These small editorial benefits do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality; the methods, empirical evidence, technical documentation, and limitations are unchanged.
